findings.description: `load_checkpoint()` restores `self.state.current_round` directly from checkpoint field `completed_round` without reconciling it against the actually reconstructed `all_findings` and `round_records`. If `checkpoint.json` is partially stale/corrupt but still parseable — e.g. `completed_round=9` while only rounds 0..7 exist in `all_findings` / `round_records` — the brain enters a self-inconsistent state. Directed-message relay uses `self.state.current_round` to decide which messages are "last round only", while other code uses `round_records[-1].round_idx` and list lengths. This can suppress valid prior-round directed messages or misalign subsequent orchestration round numbering after recovery.
findings.proposed_fix: Derive `current_round` from reconstructed round data, and only fall back to `completed_round` when no rounds were restored. Also validate consistency and log/repair mismatches.

findings.description: `verify_chain()` never validates that epoch `sealed_at` timestamps are syntactically valid RFC3339/UTC values. Record timestamps are normalized on append and effectively checked when recomputing `entry_hash`, but epoch timestamps are accepted as arbitrary strings. A tampered chain can therefore contain malformed or misleading epoch times while still passing full verification, weakening auditability of seal events.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse and normalize each epoch's `sealed_at` through `_normalize_timestamp()` during `_verify_epoch()` and require the stored value to already be in canonical UTC form.

findings.description: `_normalize_timestamp()` rejects valid ISO-8601/RFC3339 UTC timestamps that use lowercase `z`. The function only special-cases a trailing uppercase `Z`, then falls through to `datetime.fromisoformat(ts)` for all other inputs. Python's parser rejects lowercase `z`, so semantically valid UTC timestamps such as `2026-04-05T12:34:56z` fail verification/loading paths unexpectedly. This is an interface correctness bug in timestamp normalization.
findings.proposed_fix: Accept both trailing `Z` and `z` as UTC designators before parsing.

findings.description: Checkpoint recovery loses the true round/file correspondence whenever persisted rounds are sparse or non-zero-based, because `load_checkpoint()` rebuilds `RoundRecord`s by `enumerate(self.state.all_findings)` instead of the persisted `round_idx`. It then loads `round_{enumerated:02d}.json` rather than `round_{stored_round_idx:02d}.json`, and replays findings into the convergence detector under the wrong round number. This corrupts recovered model responses, round numbering, and convergence history after any missing round, partial persistence, or externally trimmed checkpoint.
findings.proposed_fix: Reconstruct round records from the persisted `round_records` entries keyed by their actual `round_idx`, load `all_findings` into a map by stored round index, and replay convergence using those real indices in sorted order.

findings.description: Metric computation assumes list index == round number. After checkpoint recovery with non-dense rounds—or even before, if persist is ever called out of sequence—`compute_metrics()` reads and writes the wrong round’s data because it uses positional indexing into `self.state.all_findings` and `self.state.round_records`. This produces incorrect `findings_this_round` and can attach metrics to the wrong `RoundRecord`.
findings.proposed_fix: Look up round data by `RoundRecord.round_idx` rather than list position. Build a round-indexed mapping for findings and update the matching `RoundRecord` by searching on its stored `round_idx`.

findings.description: The verification-chain CLI can create hash-only records that later fail full-chain verification, because `append_record()` omits `payload` from the sealed body when `storage_mode == "hash_only"`, but `_verify_single()` only checks the payload hash for `full_payload` and never verifies that a hash-only sealed body actually omitted `payload`. A tampered or malformed JSON chain can therefore include a `payload` field inside a `hash_only` record without being rejected, violating the storage-mode contract the chain claims to seal.
findings.proposed_fix: In `_verify_single()`, enforce both sides of the storage-mode invariant: `full_payload` records must contain `payload`, and `hash_only` records must not contain `payload`.

FIND: `bench/immune_agents.py`, `_verify_search_manifest()` Read step verification accepts any file that exists on the filesystem, not just files within `source_paths`. Evidence: the check is `os.path.isfile(file_arg) or file_arg in source_set or os.path.basename(file_arg) in source_basenames`.
